data.title: Leo building on Francis' legacy while reincorporating 'more traditional elements of papal activity'
data.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Miles Pattenden, historian of the Catholic Church at the University of Oxford. For Pattenden, Pope Leo XIV’s visit to France is part of a broader recalibration of the papacy. While Pope Francis placed particular emphasis on the Catholic Church’s peripheries and the needs of the Global South, Leo is subtly bringing the Church’s historic European heartlands back into focus. France is especially significant in this regard, given its deep historical relationship with Catholicism and its evolving relationship with Christianity, European identity, secularism and contemporary geopolitical debates.

data.title: ‘I sleep with all my clothes on to protect my privacy’: a glimpse into life inside a child prison in France
data.description: Photographer Alexandre Bagdassarian spent eight months following the daily lives of children in a prison system criticised for the long time spent in cells The cells of the children were difficult places for me to photograph because they are impersonal and intimate at the same time. Once inside, you quickly find yourself going in circles, with nowhere to go. Your gaze settles on the very few elements that make up the space: a window, cell bars, a rudimentary bed, a plank serving as a desk, and sometimes a book or a few drawings. Sometimes, due to staff shortages, a young person may spend as much as 23 hours a day in their cell. This and the low levels of access to educational and sports activities have been criticised by Europe’s Committee for the Prevention of Torture. The cell windows directly overlook the prison yard, a mandatory one-hour stop each day Continue reading...

data.title: Switzerland’s love of referendums keeps the far right at bay | Joseph de Weck
data.description: Brexit gave direct democracy a bad name. But the Swiss approach could be what Europe needs now Fascism rests on a two-part confidence trick. First, a leader claims to embody the will of the people. Then they argue that only by being granted sweeping powers can that be realised. Having grown up in Switzerland, I find it easy to see through this trick. That is because the policies championed by the far right rarely pass the referendum test. Dismantling publicly funded media? In March, 62% of Swiss voters rejected a far-right initiative to halve funding for the country’s public broadcaster. Corporate tax cuts? In 2017, 59% struck down such plans of the Swiss government. Immigration police hunting down migrants? Again, 59% rejected a far-right proposal to automatically deport foreign nationals convicted of crimes without judicial review. Or this week’s resounding 70% “No” vote on a far-right proposal to tighten Switzerland’s neutrality to the point that Bern would have been forced to drop sanctions on Russia over Ukraine. Joseph de Weck is an associate fellow with the German Council on Foreign Relations and writes for Guardian Europe from Zürich and Paris Continue reading...

data.title: The one change that worked: Anxiety had me hiding from the world – then two magic questions set me free
data.description: I used to be terrified of socialising, certain I would embarrass myself the moment I opened my mouth. And as for dates … As with a lot of teenagers, social confidence was not my strong suit. Throughout my time at school in the early 2010s, I hated the prospect of new social situations and would often lie awake at night overthinking the day to come. What I now know to be social anxiety I dismissed as just nerves at that young age. Although I knew something wasn’t quite right, for most of my early teens I managed to disguise my discomfort. Sharing a friendship group with my twin sister meant I could hide behind my sibling. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘The same struggles as 100 years ago’: exhibition highlights lives of Sami people in Sweden
data.description: Show at Kin Museum in Kiruna marks handover of long-awaited report on abuses committed by the state against the Indigenous people From a detailed multi-perspectival drawing of reindeer to written accounts of belief systems and childbirth, Johan Turi’s work offers unparalleled insight into his life as a Sami person living in northern Sweden at the start of the 20th century. In the face of racist discrimination, land disputes and the spectre of encroaching industry, Turi wanted his 1910 book Muitalus sámiid birra (An Account of the Sami) to set the record straight about the lives of Europe’s only recognised Indigenous people. data.title: Children forced to give up school for work as fighting upends daily life in Yemen
data.description: Renewed fighting between Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces has shattered four years of relative calm In the mornings, 13-year-old Muneer Farie went to school, and in the afternoons he helped his father feed the livestock. He took his studies seriously, dreaming of becoming the first teacher in his family of farmers. As fighting approached his village in al-Wazeyah district in Taiz, Yemen, two weeks ago, Muneer’s focus started to drift from his lessons. The classroom echoed with the distant sounds of explosions and gunfire. His home was suddenly on the frontline of renewed fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government. Continue reading...

data.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Dennis the terrier – who once farted on Jilly Cooper’s sofa
data.description: It seemed like a good idea to get a puppy with my partner, but then he left me. Single life was hard at first but my disobedient dog made me laugh again In the spring of 2024, my boyfriend and I lay in bed scrolling through photos of puppies. What about this one? Or that one? We had only been dating for six months or so, but had become besotted quickly, making long-term plans and talking about our future. Then I found the one: a scruffy, small terrier with black and brown markings on his back that looked like the world map and eyes like Galaxy Minstrels. We named him Dennis to connect him to my mum’s terrier, Beano, because she was ill at the time and I’d failed to provide her with a grandchild. A puppy was the consolation present. data.title: Sex, drugs and floral fabrics: Celia Birtwell relives her wild times – and wilder outfits – with Ossie Clark
data.description: They dressed – and partied with – the innermost in-crowd. As a swirling new show celebrates their fashion creations, Birtwell recalls her happy days with Clark and her sorrow at the loss of David Hockney In the mythical age of bohemia, the psychedelic decade between Mary Quant’s cheerful miniskirts and the first snarls of punk, Celia Birtwell and Ossie Clark were London’s most fashionable couple. Birtwell created the fabrics: daydreamy, botanical doodles that captured the idealism and looseness of the times in wisps of chiffon. Clark magicked these into sensual bias-cut dresses with a freewheeling grandeur that was part Hollywood glamour, part rock’n’roll anarchy. More than just designers, they were a whole vibe. They dressed – and partied with – the innermost of the in-crowd. Talitha Getty, Marianne Faithfull and Anita Pallenberg hung out at Quorum, their Chelsea boutique. At a catwalk show in 1970, there were two Beatles, Cecil Beaton and Brigitte Bardot in the audience – and, after Clark began making stage clothes for Mick Jagger, he accompanied the Rolling Stones on tour. David Hockney’s portrait of the couple in their pomp – Mr and Mrs Clark and Percy, painted two years into their marriage, when Birtwell was pregnant with their second child – sealed their place in the mythology of the period. data.translatedTitle: Sex, drugs and floral fabrics: Celia Birtwell relives her wild times – and wilder outfits – with Ossie Clark
data.translatedDescription: They dressed – and partied with – the innermost in-crowd. As a swirling new show celebrates their fashion creations, Birtwell recalls her happy days with Clark and her sorrow at the loss of David Hockney In the mythical age of bohemia, the psychedelic decade between Mary Quant’s cheerful miniskirts and the first snarls of punk, Celia Birtwell and Ossie Clark were London’s most fashionable couple. Birtwell created the fabrics: daydreamy, botanical doodles that captured the idealism and looseness of the times in wisps of chiffon. Clark magicked these into sensual bias-cut dresses with a freewheeling grandeur that was part Hollywood glamour, part rock’n’roll anarchy. More than just designers, they were a whole vibe. They dressed – and partied with – the innermost of the in-crowd. Talitha Getty, Marianne Faithfull and Anita Pallenberg hung out at Quorum, their Chelsea boutique. At a catwalk show in 1970, there were two Beatles, Cecil Beaton and Brigitte Bardot in the audience – and, after Clark began making stage clothes for Mick Jagger, he accompanied the Rolling Stones on tour. David Hockney’s portrait of the couple in their pomp – Mr and Mrs Clark and Percy, painted two years into their marriage, when Birtwell was pregnant with their second child – sealed their place in the mythology of the period. data.title: ‘I’ve never watched a whole episode of Peep Show’: Matt King on surviving a stroke and reviving Super Hans
data.description: The actor is returning to his character in the cult Channel 4 sitcom with a new autobiography – despite barely watching the series. He talks about his ‘terrifying’ hospital stay and why strangers still shout at him about crack being ‘moreish’ Super Hans is back! What’s he been up to since we last saw him? Splitting up with Molly , the twins, the moped -rental business in Macedonia … Well, Super Hans finds a legal loophole in the marriage certificate, which means it’s null and void and … hang on … I’m basically telling you the whole plot of the book! Is the book just you, Matt King, writing on behalf of Super Hans? Or does your inner Super Hans just come out and write it for you? It’s neither. He comes around my house every morning. I put the kettle on, he borrows my computer and off he goes. I don’t know what he gets up to. I usually try to get out of the way, go for a nice walk. Continue reading...

data.title: Is it true that … double-dipping food is unhygienic?
data.description: This practice does transmit mouth bacteria, but don’t panic Double-dipping means eating part of a piece of food and then putting it back into a communal dip – for example, biting a carrot and dipping it into shared hummus, or redipping a half-eaten tortilla chip in salsa. The concern is that bacteria from your mouth get transferred into the dip and could cause illness in the people you’re sharing it with. “You do transmit bacteria from the food you have eaten back into the source,” says Prof John Tregoning, the author of Live Forever? A Curious Scientist’s Guide to Wellness, Ageing and Death . He points to a study testing salsa, chocolate sauce and cheese dip, which found bacteria were transferred to all three, with salsa showing the most contamination. Continue reading...

data.title: AI leaders have known about the extinction threat for decades | Judith Levine
data.description: Scientists and entrepreneurs knew the dangers of AI a quarter-century ago. But animated by curiosity and profit, they went ahead anyway Over the past few weeks, many of us have struggled to concoct a mental image of brains in the cloud jumping their “sandbox”, sneaking onto the internet, recruiting “swarms” of other “agents” to cheat on a test, and, after discussing the ethics of the act, hacking into a wiki platform with the weird name Hugging Face. We knew that artificial intelligence was devouring our jobs, degrading our kids’ education, and deepfaking our politics; that datacenters were sucking up our water and electricity and sending us the bills. But until 8 September, when the Anthropic computer scientist Jacob Coxon posted his existential terror on Twitter/X, few of us suspected AI might be endangering our survival. Continue reading...

data.title: Forget the famous names. Here is who actually deserves this year’s Nobel peace prize | Haakon Gjerløw
data.description: The betting markets favour the US president and Volodymyr Zelenskyy. But the most vital work to secure peace is being done by those far from the spotlight Haakon Gjerløw is the acting director of the Peace Research Institute Oslo The Nobel peace prize is not a contest determined by fame. Yet the betting markets consistently gravitate towards the biggest names in global politics – among them this year, Donald Trump and Volodymyr Zelenskyy. That misses what the prize is for. The real work of building peace is often done far from the headlines: by courts that uphold international law, journalists who document atrocities, and humanitarian organisations that protect communities. With the 2026 prize due to be announced on 9 October, the Nobel committee has an opportunity to remind the world that peace is built through institutions and cooperation, not just diplomatic grandstanding. Continue reading...

data.title: Job interviews are a weird business – but what’s the alternative? | Emma Beddington
data.description: Given the biased nature of the interview process, the recent kerfuffle about taking iced coffee in with you may be the least of our worries I was part of a job interview process recently, on the hiring side of the table for the first time in 15 years, and was instantly reminded how weird the whole business is. The debate about whether bringing iced coffee to interviews is bad form just highlights the silliness of selection processes: you could bring a live weasel to an interview and still get the job if the interviewer likes the look of you. It’s a biased , arbitrary business, and interviewers decide fast (a 2015 study found 25% decided within five minutes and 60% within 15), sometimes on little more than vibes. Everyone has a horror story: an acquaintance was recently told she was “perfect for the role”, despite barely saying a word as the interviewer monologued wildly for 45 minutes while vaping in her face. Being a good interviewee isn’t the same as being a good employee, either. I’ve crashed and burned at every interview, including for jobs I know I would have done decently. Once my interviewers told me they knew I was messy “because we’ve seen your kitchen” (the perils of 00s blogging); another time, a junior employee informed me before the ordeal had even started that I’d blown it by wearing trousers. Continue reading...

data.title: The hill I will die on: No music, quiz nights or bustling saloon bar – pubs should have no atmosphere | Maureen Younger
data.description: Ambiance: who wants it and why do so many pubs contrive to create it? The deader the pub the better, in my view I was out with a mate one evening when she asked where I’d like to go. My response was immediate: “A pub with no atmosphere.” I cannot think of anywhere better. You get served straight away, you get a seat and, if you’re really lucky, there’s no music. Seriously, what’s not to like? First things first: by “pub”, I mean the old-fashioned type, with carpets that stick to the soles of your shoes – no gastropub nonsense. I’m still fuming from the time I ordered fish and chips in one of these (unbeknown to me) gastropubs. It’s a simple meal; a British staple. How can you get that wrong? Well first, the fish and peas arrived on a slate slab (an item, by all rights, I should only come across in my dad’s shed). I’m no physicist, but if a dish contains peas, then having a totally flat surface to place them on is not ideal. Worse, for some inexplicable reason the chips had been separated from the fish and placed in a metal container, which, as I discovered when I foolhardily attempted to pick it up, was hot enough to cause third-degree burns. When I quite reasonably asked if they could not just bung everything on a plate, the look of disdain would have you believe I had asked the barman if I could abduct his first-born child. Continue reading...

data.title: Is your kid off to a sleepover? Don’t forget the secret codeword | Polly Hudson
data.description: Sometimes a child needs to say ‘I’m having a horrible time!’ without everyone around them realising. Ukulele! The second you have a baby, people begin offering you unsolicited advice. Friends, acquaintances and – most fun of all – complete strangers you definitely didn’t ask will inform you that your child isn’t dressed warmly enough, or that you have to enjoy every moment. I once had the latter while my two-month-old was spraying me with liquids from both ends, which the wise sage had apparently not noticed. In the sea of interfering nonsense is the odd genuinely useful life raft, though, such as one I’ve just learned for dealing with the tween period I’m now navigating. Your child needs not a coat, but a codeword. Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on Manchester City: a strange kind of glory | Editorial
data.description: If a guilty verdict on multiple counts of financial misreporting is upheld against the club, its achievements in the modern era will be forever tainted In surveys ranking the Premier League’s greatest moments, football supporters regularly give pride of place to Sergio Agüero’s championship-winning goal for Manchester City in 2012. Scored in injury time on the last day of the season, Agüero’s strike against Queens Park Rangers delivered the first league title for City since the 1960s. Knocking their historic rivals Manchester United into second place, it also signalled a new era in which the club replaced United as the dominant force in the English game. “Aguerooooooo!” – the incredulous single-word response from the match commentator Martin Tyler – has entered football folklore. But an asterisk may now be needed at the end of all those Os. Reports that an independent panel has found Manchester City guilty of breaking Premier League rules between 2009 and 2023 cast a dark shadow over that day, and much else besides. During that period, the club won seven Premier League titles, six League Cups, three FA Cups and the Uefa Champions League, all while under the ownership of Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, a member of the Abu Dhabi ruling family. The inescapable implication of the apparent ruling is that those trophies were won unfairly. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Arsène Wenger and Arsenal: 30 years on from appointment that changed English football
data.description: David Dein’s decision to hire the Frenchman ushered in an irreversible era of multiculturalism, giving birth to the Premier League we know today As feedback goes, even a character as relentlessly optimistic as David Dein might have considered the reaction to his bold managerial appointment suboptimal. Thirty years ago, Arsenal were in a state of chaotic flux, having sacked Bruce Rioch, with the interims Stewart Houston and Pat Rice in charge. There had been talk of Johan Cruyff arriving and Dein wanted to fill the information vacuum. Summoning the team, he reassured them a new manager would soon be appointed and that he was a world-class addition. “His name is Arsène Wenger,” Dein, the club’s vice-chair, beamed. A brief pause ensued before a player’s voice called out: “Who the fuck is he?” His exclamation echoed conventional wisdom. “Arsene Who?” famously read The London Evening Standard’s billboards prior to Wenger being confirmed as manager on 30 September 1996 . Continue reading...

data.title: Republic of Ireland put controversy aside to earn impressive win over Israel
data.description: Football and politics are inseparable in the modern world, no matter how many people wish they were not. But whether the beautiful game can ease the ills of our age is another matter. After a week in which the issue of Irish support for the people of Gaza had turned this fixture into a battle of conscience, the outcome of this underwhelming match ultimately felt inconsequential. In the end the result was indeed a walkover, just not because of a boycott. On Saturday night the question had been whether Heimir Hallgrimsson’s side would take to the field in Hungary at all. If they did, would their heads be in the game? It turned out that a week of internal angst had been enough to produce collective resolve among the Irish squad, or at least those selected to play. Strong and assertive from the off, their forwards each scored in the first half to settle the contest, with plenty of symbolic action to assure those back home of their feelings. Continue reading...

data.title: Nations League: Greece stun Klopp’s Germany, Netherlands sink Serbia but Gakpo hurt
data.description: Jürgen Klopp ‘unbothered’ despite 1-0 home defeat Gakpo goes off in 2-1 win, Portugal edge past Norway Greece stunned Germany 1-0 in Augsburg to go top of their Nations League group and spoil Jürgen Klopp’s debut in the home dugout. Dimitrios Kourbelis scored the only goal in the 74th minute, earning Greece their first-ever victory in 11 matches against Germany. Ivan Jovanovic’s side now lead ⁠Group A2 with six points ⁠from two matches; Klopp’s side are third with one point from two games after a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands on Thursday. data.title: OK, now it’s time for the Patriots to panic about Drake Maye
data.description: The New England quarterback was a revelation in the 2025 regular season. But Sunday’s loss was just the latest in a series of crushing lows After the Patriots pulled out a win in Week 2 over the Steelers, despite another uninspiring performance from Drake Maye, Mike Vrabel avoided answering questions about his quarterback. Vrabel joked with a reporter not to “ruin my Sunday” when asked about Maye. And this was after a win . On Sunday, Maye was largely responsible for ruining Vrabel’s afternoon in the Patriots’ 35-6 loss to Jacksonville, which felt like rock bottom (the Pats hope). Simply put, Maye was atrocious. The 2025 MVP runner-up was 14-of-25 for 199 yards, no touchdowns, two interceptions, three sacks, and a lost fumble. Continue reading...

data.title: Tony Pulis says he and Stoke were ‘cheated’ in 2011 FA Cup final after Manchester City verdict
data.description: Manchester City won match 1-0 after goal by Yaya Touré Club deny wrongdoing and say ‘process is ongoing’ Tony Pulis has said his Stoke City team were “cheated” out of the 2011 FA Cup after Manchester City were found guilty on virtually all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules. Pulis’s Stoke lost the 2011 Cup final 1-0 after Yaya Touré’s goal. Yet following Friday’s news that City are guilty on all but one of the more than 100 charges laid by the Premier League in February 2023, Pulis feels serious discontent. City are expected to appeal and they deny any wrongdoing. Continue reading...

data.title: Iran says it ‘has no plans to negotiate with US’ despite Trump claims – US politics live
data.description: Trump had told Axios he expected talks to resume a day after he rejected Iran’s proposal to reopen the strait of Hormuz Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog. State media in Iran has reported that Iran’s delegation to the UN General Assembly had no talks planned with the United States, after US president Donald Trump said he expected more negotiations. The Trump administration on Monday plans to release new fuel economy standards that would relax regulatory requirements for automakers to control pollution from gasoline-powered cars and light trucks. President Donald Trump said on his Truth Social media account on Saturday that the less stringent mileage requirements would “take the waste out of building cars in America” and save families “thousands on a new, beautiful and safe car,” while boosting auto production in the US. Donald Trump ’s attorney general Todd Blanche argued on Sunday that the administration was permitted to ban three news outlets from the White House because “it is a privilege and not a right to be there”. Appearing on the ABC News program This Week during the second week of the White House’s dispute over press credentialing and access, Blanche also said that the administration took the decision to ban CNN, MS Now and Politico beginning on 19 September because the president was “sick and tired” of what he considered to be those media outlets’ inaccurate reporting. US senator Thom Tillis on Sunday criticized Donald Trump , his fellow Republican, for the president’s support of Ken Paxton over incumbent John Cornyn in the Texas Senate Republican primary. “He made a colossal mistake,” Tillis, a frequent Trump critic from North Carolina, said during an interview on CNN’s State of the Union in reference to the president’s support of Paxton who defeated Cornyn in the May primary. The United States and China released Monday reciprocal lists of products worth about $30bn each that will see tariff cuts, in a deal expected to boost bilateral trade. The details came days after Chinese President Xi Jinping met with president Donald Trump in Washington in his first state visit to the US since 2015. Trump justified the pending US arms sale to Taiwan to Chinese president Xi Jinping by downplaying it as just one of many sales Washington makes around the world - even asking Xi if he’d be in the market for US arms, Trump’s ambassador to China said on Sunday. House Democrats are preparing a vast oversight agenda, with investigations of Trump, his family and his administration if the party sweeps control of the chamber from Republicans in the November elections. The undertaking is as robust as it is daunting, spanning several House committees. Continue reading...

data.title: Swiss voters reject stricter neutrality rules that would have curbed Nato cooperation
data.description: 70% vote against tightening centuries-old neutrality, which far right said was being eroded by sanctions against Russia Swiss voters have decisively rejected a proposal for a strict definition of neutrality that would have required Switzerland to curb cooperation with Nato and abandon sanctions against Russia. All cantons and about 70% of voters rejected the proposal for a strictly defined version of neutrality to be ⁠written into the Swiss constitution, final results from the Federal Statistical Office showed. The motion had been promoted by the far-right Swiss People’s party (SVP). Continue reading...

data.title: Serbia’s populist president Aleksandar Vučić resigns to run for prime minister
data.description: Vučić not allowed to seek third presidential term and election will test his grip on rule after widespread protests Serbia’s populist president, Aleksandar Vučić, has resigned to pursue an attempt to become prime minister in an early parliamentary election that will test his firm rule in the Balkan country after nearly two years of protests. Vučić’s second presidential term would otherwise end in May next year. He is banned by the constitution from seeking a third term and said he was resigning to lead his rightwing Serbian Progressive party (SNS) in the 25 October ballot. Continue reading...

data.title: Bangkok declared a ‘disaster zone’ after flooding, as rainstorms shift direction
data.description: Capital city submerged in waist-high flood water, while elsewhere Hurricane Nolo threatens Hawaii’s Big Island Bangkok was declared a disaster zone by its city officials towards the end of last week, after streets in Thailand’s capital city were submerged in up to waist-high flood water. The flooding stemmed from an active cell of low pressure across central Thailand that brought continuous heavy rainfall and thunderstorms to Bangkok and surrounding regions. The heavy rain began early on Thursday when the weak area of low pressure travelled north-westwards up the gulf of Thailand before then sitting over central Thailand by Friday morning. For most of the following two days this low pressure remained roughly in situ, which allowed unrelenting downpours over Bangkok and nearby areas. One weather station near Prachin Buri, just north-east of the capital, recorded 213.5mm within a 24-hour period between Friday and Saturday evening local time – for comparison, London receives an average 585mm a year ). Fortunately, the centre of the low-pressure cell shifted north-westwards on Sunday and brought an end to the torrential rainfall. Continue reading...

data.title: The UK wildfire investigators: ‘If someone has used a match, chances are you’ll find it’
data.description: Scientists are racing to understand how fires behave to predict and prevent them as hotter summers create tinderboxes From the scorched heathlands of the New Forest to the smouldering valleys of south Wales and burned-out homes in Stourbridge , an extraordinary summer of wildfires has left its mark across Britain. To most of us, these charred landscapes may look like pure devastation, but to a trained wildfire investigator they are full of clues. Heat-scorched leaves can become frozen in position, preserving evidence of the wind direction as the fire passed through. Soot or staining on rocks, the pattern of fallen grass and bracken, and even how those stems have burned, provide further information about how the fire itself moved. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘You can taste the land’: the Somerset farmer bringing wildflowers back to cheddar
data.description: Tom Calver has sacrificed milk yields to give his cows a more varied diet of plants and believes the result is better cheese and richer farmland In the rolling hills of Somerset, hundreds of thousands of cows placidly munch lush green grass to produce milk for cheddar. But six fields stand out. Rather than uniform grass, they have technicolour wildflowers sprouting across the meadows. Farmer Tom Calver said that to allow the flowers to grow he has to keep fewer cows and leave some fields ungrazed as they mature. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces’: Cape Town divided over plan to remove its monkeys
data.description: Two troops of chacma baboons are breaking into homes and shops but animal rights activists insist coexistence is the answer Cape Town’s city council has said it will “imminently” round up two baboon troops coming into repeated conflict with residents . The animals will be sterilised and permanently moved to a newly constructed sanctuary. The plan has been fiercely criticised by animal rights activists, who say the monkeys should remain roaming freely, and that less destructive options have not been properly considered. Cape Town’s baboon problem has been brewing since the 2000s, after the city stopped culling troops in the late 1990s after pressure from the public. But in the past two years it has reached boiling point. A 2025 census found that the population had grown by a third since 2000, from 360 baboons to 493, now living in 12 managed troops. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘My husband has to remind me: You’re not a real cop!’ Siân Brooke on the perils of playing a tough Blue Lights ‘peeler’
data.description: She lit up Sherlock, made a brutal exit from House of the Dragon and now she’s back in the hard-hitting Belfast-set police drama. Will she have to stuff a chopping board into her flak jacket this time round? Sharp eyes save lives. That’s the mantra of the police officers in Blue Lights, although the words sound a good deal more urgent when said in a throaty Belfast accent. The city, dealing with past and present problems, is the turbulent setting for the hit drama. Having starred in the BBC series for the past four years, Siân Brooke has taken its lessons about vigilance to heart. “I noticed some dodgy-looking activity not far from where we live in London,” says Brooke. “I’d driven past a few times and was suspicious. I told my husband that the last time I went past, I slowed down and did a drive-by, so they’d know their untoward behaviour had been rumbled. My husband said: ‘You can’t do that, Siân. You’re not a real cop!’” She laughs. “I think Blue Lights has got to me. What was I going to do, make a citizen’s arrest?” Continue reading...

data.title: Korea review – a nirvana of wild beauty shattered by the 20th century
data.description: British Museum, London The staggering resourcefulness and fantastic originality of bygone artisans is showcased in earthenware so exquisite it will soothe your soul. But a lurch into the modern breaks the spell Can they do it again? The runaway success of the Bayeux tapestry has put the British Museum in a league of its own, perhaps making it, at this moment, the leading museum on earth – and it’s rapidly following up with Korea, a survey of “2,000 years of creativity” in a land that, before its sufferings in the 20th century, enjoyed millennia of calm, at least to judge from its art. But it’s a blockbuster with a tragic flaw, a lovely broken vase badly stuck together. You are lured at first into a nirvana of beauty. A giant bronze bell from a Buddhist monastery, cast in the eighth century AD and bulging with dragons, flames and flowery embossments, strikes the tone. It calls you to meditation. A gong adds to the harmony (and if you need that underlining, there are bells and gongs on the now obligatory exhibition soundtrack). I was held rapt by this Buddhist period in Korea’s history, when the contemplative religion from India interacted with the artistic influence of China to inspire ecstatic hand-copied sutras (spiritual scriptures) and slender little statuettes of bodhisattvas (Buddhist saints who have achieved enlightened holiness). Continue reading...

data.title: Crushed review – Steve Oram is priestly lead in harrowing Bangkok-set child-abduction thriller
data.description: A priest investigates his daughter’s kidnapping in Thailand in this Paul Schrader-esque inquiry into spiritual nihilism ‘He’s American, a little bit overweight, sweaty, a little bit camp, creepy.” As far as descriptions of border-hopping paedophiles go, this seems a little on the nose. So it’s not surprising when the man who was enquiring, priest Father Daniel (Steve Oram), responds: “Are you making this up?” Featuring a seedy child-abduction situation in Bangkok, Simon Rumley’s thriller comes close at times to bugged-out exploitation flick territory – but lets its fleet and fresh manner carry it towards a Paul Schrader-esque moral calvary. Pastor to a mixed Anglo-Thai congregation, Father Daniel has a young daughter, Olivia (Margaux Dietrich), with wife May (Nattapohn Rawddon). At a sleepover, Olivia is traumatised when her friend’s older brother shows her a “crush” video of a kitten being stomped by a scantily clad floozy. So when her own cat Missy goes awol, she is convinced the same lady is responsible, and asks her dad how God could let it happen. The family mobilise to track down Missy, but Olivia in turn disappears one day after school, kicking off Father Daniel’s own test of faith. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Should have garnered the actor an Oscar’: why Liar Liar is my feelgood movie
data.description: The latest in our series of writers paying tribute to the films they watch when they need a lift is an appreciation of Jim Carrey’s manic 90s comedy To be completely honest, whenever anybody asks what my favorite movies are, my list has some typical standbys: Goodfellas and It’s a Wonderful Life among them. The holiday classic National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation is another. But there’s one feelgood fave on my list that always surprises people: Jim Carrey’s 1997 blockbuster Liar Liar. The movie (for the lack of a better word) lies on the bedrock of a simple premise: a lawyer and doting father is physically unable to tell an untruth due to a birthday wish. In the hands of a less competent creative team and cast, Liar Liar would have been yet another forgettable piece of 90s comedy junk; destined for the bottom of a discount VHS bin, forgotten as the years trudged on. But largely thanks to an unbelievable performance courtesy of Carrey, who was working with a smart and peppy script, the film thusly ascends into rarefied air. Continue reading...

data.title: Just Play Dead review – Samuel L Jackson and Eva Green punch up switchback crime caper
data.description: Jackson and Green just about manage to distract viewers from the sub-par Tarantinoesque flourishes, confusing plot points and tired stereotypes Having shot five films since 2020, 82-year-old Martin Campbell is a certified member of the post-retirement director’s club that includes Ridley Scott, Martin Scorsese, Woody Allen et al. Samuel L Jackson (a mere 77) sports his worst hairdo since Jackie Brown – a grey, crimped ponytail with an undercut – in this overworked crime caper, though he is on positively cuddly form by his standards. Interrupting his retirement on a Spanish-speaking Caribbean island with the odd poisoning (seen in the intro), kingpin Jack Wolfe (Jackson) is getting antsy. Afraid the law is close behind him, he hatches a scheme with his philandering wife Nora (Eva Green): help him frame her surfer lover Chad (Jason Fernández) for his supposed murder, and they will split the big-bucks insurance payout. He covers his back for the possibility she might do him in for real by recording her saying as much. But she ropes Chad anyway into her murder conspiracy, plotting to let him take the fall – or perhaps her detective bit on the side Dani (Eoin Macken) will get there first. Continue reading...

data.title: Range by Dorthe Nors review – an astrophysicist at odds with reality
data.description: In the Danish writer’s latest novel, an eminent scientist withdraws to the countryside When Gunn Haven, an eminent professor of astrophysics at an urban university, moves to rural Denmark, she tells a local newspaper: “It’s to do with the sky.” From the outset of Range, Danish author Dorthe Nors’s fifth full-length novel, it is apparent this is not the whole truth. Soon after arriving, Gunn is compelled to trespass along a nearby track to look at a farmhouse with collapsed gable walls, her curiosity driven by personal interest rather than scientific inquiry. A woman pulls up in a dark blue BMW. She is dressed in “hunter’s camouflage, fleshy-faced. And ponytailed. Weapon raised: a phone, filming Gunn.” Gunn reluctantly retreats. Gunn is distracted by this woman, Krista, who works at the local potato flour factory. Gunn should be working on a general introduction to astrophysics, “the Work”. Instead, the Professor finds herself wondering what “Gable Woman” would do if she came to “the Institute”, where Gunn researches “light from the oldest galaxies”. She would draw a dick on a blackboard, Gunn imagines, “with a small titillated smile”. Gunn is more generous to promising young scientists. She pays for a former student to travel to America. Closer to home, she begins to help Jenny, the teenage daughter of her hairdresser, with a school project on black holes. Jenny is an “uneducated creature” who smells “faintly of iron”, with a “faint red to the cheeks, from shyness or cold. Oddly sexless, and she had been here before, but with her mother.” Continue reading...

data.title: Deep into the Sixties: Britain 1965-66 by David Kynaston review – a tour de force of popular history
data.description: From the Beatles and the World Cup to racism and homophobia, the latest instalment in Kynaston’s series captures a society in the throes of change In February 1965, the civil rights activist Malcolm X visited Smethwick, in the Midlands, where the Conservative-run council was planning to buy up houses to stop the area becoming a “coloured ghetto”. He wanted to see how bad the racism was and he experienced it first-hand when refused service in a pub. White residents thought his visit a “disgusting” intrusion. Nine days later, back in the US, he was shot dead. Britain in the mid-60s is associated with Carnaby Street, the Beatles and miniskirts, not racism. But what Black people endured, from a colour bar on property to the abuse of Leeds United winger Albert Johanneson as a “golliwog”, is no less a period marker than Harold Wilson’s pipe, Twiggy’s haircut, Mary Whitehouse’s clean-up TV campaign and Bob Dylan’s use of an electric guitar. David Kynaston doesn’t underplay the excitements of the period. But he rightly emphasises that the rotten old 50s – patriarchal, homophobic, class-divided and bigoted – wouldn’t just fade away. Multi-flavoured Golden Wonder crisps displacing Smith’s plain; one-third of new marriages now civil marriages; pubs reluctantly installing fruit machines; Jimmy Hill’s Sky-Blue revolution at Coventry City; AA patrols no longer required to salute; picture rails, seen as dust traps, removed en masse from Victorian and Edwardian houses; Boots from 1965 at last consenting to sell condoms; arrival of open-plan offices; arrival, too, of the hot drinks vending machine; no car more iconic of modernity than the Mini Cooper … Continue reading...

data.title: Tomi Adeyemi on the film of her hit novel Children of Blood and Bone: ‘I don’t plan to watch it’
data.description: Her debut earned a record-breaking YA book deal – then came her fallout with Hollywood. The author talks about the pressures of success and why she is pictured on the cover of her new novel There is a photograph of Tomi Adeyemi staring out from the cover of her new novel, The Siren. It is an arresting image: her face fills the frame, unsoftened by a smile, her piercing gaze fixed directly on the viewer. “It’s terrifying – like the Mona Lisa, staring at you everywhere,” she says, laughing. Using an author portrait on the cover of a novel is highly unusual, and a decision that Adeyemi says is a statement of ownership. After 12 years spent inside the world of Children of Blood and Bone – the first book in the YA trilogy that made her a literary star and its film adaptation which has become a source of profound distress – Adeyemi wanted this book to belong unmistakably to her. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘The champagne of pale ales’: my search for the perfect kölsch beer in Cologne
data.description: ‘Kölsch is not a drink, it is a religion’ in Cologne, and it’s only brewed in and around the German city. But which of the many beautiful, storied beer halls serves up the best? There’s a saying in Cologne, repeated with the mild smugness of people who know they’re right: kölsch is the only culture you can drink. It sounds like a line lifted straight from the tourist board’s brochure. Then you spend a day working your way around the city’s traditional brewhouses and realise it’s a statement of fact. Since 1997, kölsch has held a protected geographical indication within the EU, guaranteeing that any beer bearing the name is brewed within 50km of the city and made strictly to the Kölsch-Konvention. That agreement, signed in 1986, defined the style as “ a light, highly attenuated, hop-accentuated, clear, top-fermenting ‘vollbier’ [full-beer] ”, restricting production exclusively to the local area. It is, in effect, the champagne of pale ales: locally adored and tied to a city that has always insisted on doing things its own way. Continue reading...

data.title: With turbulence all around, Armani plays it safe and easy in Milan
data.description: The late designer’s niece echoes his sense of relaxation, as the house seeks to prove itself to potential buyers A year after the death of Giorgio Armani, the Italian fashion house he founded in 1975 is facing increasing uncertainty about its future ownership. In his will, Armani, who ruled over the business for 50 years, instructed his heirs to sell an initial 15% stake of the company within 18 months of his death. If a private sale does not materialise, an IPO is mandated to take place. Now there are reports the group is readying itself for formal talks with the French conglomerate LVMH, the beauty giant L’Oréal and the eyewear group EssilorLuxottica – three of Armani’s preferred acquirers – over the possible sale of a minority stake. Continue reading...

data.title: Does GLP-1 use result in significant hair loss?
data.description: Experts share what you need to know about GLP-1-related hair loss as the side-effect gets more attention from researchers About 20 million people across the US , UK, and EU are taking GLP-1 receptor agonists like tirzepatide and semaglutide (Ozempic or Mounjaro are common brands) for weight loss and type 2 diabetes. As their use has surged, we’re learning more about their side-effects. One that’s been getting a lot of attention from researchers lately: hair loss. In one survey of people who take these medications, 20% of respondents experienced hair shedding, although the lack of high-quality data from a randomized, controlled trial to assess this side-effect makes it difficult to know exactly how common it is. Continue reading...

data.title: The endangered native ponies of Eriskay in the Outer Hebrides – a photo essay
data.description: Fewer than 400 Eriskay ponies remain. One of the rarest native breeds in the world, their plight is unique because the community living on their tiny Hebridean island are fighting for them. The ponies wander the village and townsfolk care for them together On the slopes of Beinn Sciathan, a rocky outcrop in the Outer Hebrides, white and grey ponies roam freely. Eriskay ponies, one of the rarest native breeds in the world, are critically endangered. They have often been mixed with the Highland pony and other breeds, giving the false impression of higher population numbers. Only about 300 to 400 Eriskay ponies are thought to remain. Continue reading...

data.title: Late-night drive and a 999 call: farmer’s chance encounter that led to terrorism arrests at RAF base
data.description: Local people say members of WhatsApp group noticed suspicious activity around vans in Whelford overnight In the early hours of Sunday morning, a resident of the village of Whelford was driving home from a party when she saw three white vans parked on a country road. She was immediately suspicious, she said, and all the more so when she spotted a “large group of hooded and balaclavaed” men. She called 999 and police arrived on the scene 15 minutes later. The resident, who asked not to be named but reportedly is a local farmer, told the Press Association: “It would appear that by doing so I just derailed whatever they [the men] were planning. A plucky amateur shouldn’t be spotting an unusual bit of activity at 1am when the airbase is on high alert. I think it’s absolutely astonishing.” Continue reading...

data.title: At age 6, Grace opened a lemonade stand hoping to raise $10, seven summers later, she made $55,000
data.description: Grace Hendrian and her sister June initiated their Lemon-Aid Stand for Good in 2019 to support charity. They aimed to raise $10 but ultimately collected $55,000 for The Salvation Army. Their project encouraged community participation, leading to 14 stands operating by 2026. The sisters received recognition for their volunteer efforts as they also contributed to local families in need. Their fundraising initiative concluded in 2026, marking its final season.

data.title: In 2024, Iowa farmer Evie Haupt earned $35,000 yearly from 3 turbines, cutting debt to $67,000
data.description: Evie Haupt, an Iowa farmer, has notably increased her revenue by leasing land for wind turbines. This extra income has been instrumental in alleviating her farm debts following her husband's passing. Even though the turbines occupy less than an acre, she continues her traditional farming practices on the bulk of her land. The rise of wind power is transforming the financial prospects for rural landowners nationwide.

data.description: Quando um filhote de chimpanzé morre, a mãe o carrega nas costas por dias, semanas ou até mesmo meses. O mesmo acontece entre os bonobos, outra espécie do gênero Pan, parentes mais próximos dos humanos. Este é um comportamento que intriga cientistas há décadas e levanta questionamentos sobre o quão conscientes sobre a morte essas espécies talvez sejam. Leia mais (09/28/2026 - 06h00)

data.title: Putins nya plan: Massiva anfall med jetdrönare i vinter

I stället satsar han nu på att med massiva anfall med billiga, jetdrivna drönare, tvinga Ukraina att kapitulera denna vinter, enligt en ny analys. Då slipper han dessutom en ny, impopulär mobilisering.
data.translatedTitle: Putin's new plan: Massive strikes with jet drones this winter
data.translatedDescription: Russian President Vladimir Putin may have abandoned the idea of ​​wearing down Ukraine through an endless war of attrition, where they occupy the country meter by meter. Then he also avoids a new, unpopular mobilization.

data.translatedTitle: Tomas Ramberg: Cold war between V and S
data.translatedDescription: Magdalena Andersson's claim that the Left Party and the Moderates constitute a "new constellation" does not hold. Nevertheless, it goes without saying that the Social Democrats will strike back with force against the Left Party's tough parliamentary game. Now there is a cold war in the government issue. But there is also a well-thought-out strategy behind Andersson's move.

data.title: Riksdagen samlas för talmansval
data.description: Riksdagen samlas för första gången för att välja talman. Allt talar för att Tidöpartiernas kandidat Andreas Norlén får fortsätta, då även Vänsterpartiet meddelat sitt stöd till honom. Socialdemokraterna har nominerat Johanna Haraldsson till både talman och vice talman.
data.translatedTitle: The Riksdag gathers for the election of the Speaker
data.translatedDescription: The Riksdag gathers for the first time to elect the Speaker. Everything points to Tidöpartierna's candidate Andreas Norlén being allowed to continue, as the Left Party also announced its support for him. The Social Democrats have nominated Johanna Haraldsson for both Speaker and Deputy Speaker.

data.title: Guide inför Sverige-Polen: Skadebekymmer efter premiärsegern
data.description: Sverige fick en bra start i Nations League-fotbollen med 2–1 mot Rumänien. Måndag kväll väntar Polen på Strawberry arena. Här är en matchguide.
data.translatedTitle: Guide for Sweden-Poland: Injury concerns after the premiership victory
data.translatedDescription: Sweden got off to a good start in Nations League football with a 2-1 win against Romania. Monday evening, Poland awaits at the Strawberry arena. Here is a match guide.

data.title: Magdalena Andersson lämnar tillbaka sonderingsuppdraget
data.description: Timmar innan talmansvalet lämnar S-ledaren Magdalena Andersson tillbaka sonderingsuppdraget. Anledningen är att Vänsterpartiet ställt sig bakom Tidöpartiernas talmanskandidat Andreas Norlén (M). – Därmed har det ju bildats en ny konstellation i riksdagen av vänsterpartister och moderater, säger Magdalena Andersson vid en pressträff.
data.translatedTitle: Magdalena Andersson hands back the probe assignment
data.translatedDescription: Hours before the speaker election, S leader Magdalena Andersson gives back the probe mission. The reason is that the Left Party stood behind Tidöpartierna's speaker candidate Andreas Norlén (M). - Thus, a new constellation has been formed in the Riksdag of left-wing parties and moderates, says Magdalena Andersson at a press conference.

data.title: ”Peer Gynt” plockar russinen ur den norska nationalepos-kakan
data.description: ”Peer Gynt” på Folkteatern i Göteborg är lite som en lök – ingen kärna, bara skal. När skolade dansare möter skådespelare blir resultatet både vackert och ojämnt, skriver Isa Andersson.
data.translatedTitle: "Peer Gynt" picks the raisin from the Norwegian national epic cake
data.translatedDescription: "Peer Gynt" at Folkteatern in Gothenburg is a bit like an onion - no core, just skin. When trained dancers meet actors, the result is both beautiful and uneven, writes Isa Andersson.

data.title: Aris Fioretos stil får en grym värld att skina
data.description: En afghansk flicka flyr för sitt liv genom ett hotfullt Berlin. Jenny Aschenbrenner läser en roman full av skärande starka bilder och komplexa textflätor.
data.translatedTitle: Aris Fioreto's style makes a cruel world shine
data.translatedDescription: An Afghan girl flees for her life through a menacing Berlin. Jenny Aschenbrenner is reading a novel full of cutting strong images and complex text braids.

data.title: Insändare. Nu måste de rödgröna komma upp ur sandlådan
data.description: INSÄNDARE. Vänsterpartiets besked i talmansfrågan är en märklig signal mitt under det första försöket att bilda en ny regering. Många av oss som arbetade dag och natt för en förändring gjorde inte de för att efter valet se prestige och positionering ta över, skriver den tidigare S-riksdagsledamoten Juan Fonseca.
data.translatedTitle: Letter to the editor. Now the red-greens have to get out of the sandbox
data.translatedDescription: LETTER TO THE EDITOR. The Left Party's statement on the speaker question is a strange signal in the middle of the first attempt to form a new government. Many of us who worked day and night for a change didn't do it to see prestige and positioning take over after the election, writes the former S Riksdag member Juan Fonseca.

data.title: Olle Svenning: Förr byggdes allianser över ett glas – nu vågar man knappt prata med varandra
data.description: Regeringssamarbeten kunde formas av grannsämja, personkemi och samtal långt utanför plenisalen. Bisarrt förvisso, men mindre absurt än beröringsskräcken i det nu segrande politiska blocket, skriver Olle Svenning.
data.translatedTitle: Olle Svenning: In the past, alliances were built over a glass - now you hardly dare to talk to each other
data.translatedDescription: Government collaborations could be shaped by neighborliness, personal chemistry and conversations far outside the plenary hall. Bizarre, certainly, but less absurd than the horror of touch in the now victorious political bloc, writes Olle Svenning.

data.title: Kalena: Jag vill tacka både Miljöpartiet och Sverigedemokraterna
data.description: Kalena söker efter minsta gemensamma nämnaren i politiken. Hon hittar två skäl att simma lugnt.
data.translatedTitle: Kalena: I want to thank both the Green Party and the Sweden Democrats
data.translatedDescription: Kalena searches for the lowest common denominator in politics. She finds two reasons to swim calmly.

data.title: Bonden larmade om misstänkta terroristerna: ”Vad sjutton”
data.description: Vita skåpbilar som blockerade vägen och maskerade män som sprang bort mot skogen och flygbasen. Synen fick en bonde i Gloucestershire att larma polisen – och nu utreds förberedelse till terroristbrott. – Jag undrade bara vad sjutton de höll på med, säger kvinnan till The Telegraph.
data.translatedTitle: The farmer raised the alarm about the suspected terrorists: "What the hell"
data.translatedDescription: White vans blocking the road and masked men running away towards the forest and the air base. The sight prompted a farmer in Gloucestershire to alert the police - and now preparations for terrorist crimes are being investigated. - I just wondered what the hell they were doing, says the woman to The Telegraph.

data.title: Efva Attling: ”På Joe and the juice vet de inte vem jag är – det är så jävla skönt”
data.description: Hon fick höra att hon borde gå ner i vikt, sluta med musik och tänka om. I stället blev hon Efva Attling – med ett halvt sekel i strålkastarljuset. Nu släpper smyckesdesignern en personlig bok som rymmer alltifrån romantik till smärtsamma förluster. För DN berättar hon om kroppsideal, silversmide och den oväntade lyxen med att gå på juicebar.
data.translatedTitle: Efva Attling: "At Joe and the juice they don't know who I am - it's so damn nice"
data.translatedDescription: She was told she should lose weight, quit music and rethink. Instead, she became Efva Attling - with half a century in the spotlight. Now the jewelry designer is releasing a personal book that covers everything from romance to painful losses. For DN, she talks about body ideals, silversmithing and the unexpected luxury of going to a juice bar.

data.title: Ställdes mot favoritlaget i Premier League-debuten: ”Vad gör jag här?”
data.description: Sedan sommarens VM har den svenske landslagsmannen Elliot Stroud bytt Mjällby i allsvenskan mot Hull i Premier League. Redan i debuten fick han spela mot sitt favoritlag. – Där och då känner man: ”Vad gör jag här egentligen?”, säger Stroud.
data.translatedTitle: Faced with the favorite team in the Premier League debut: "What am I doing here?"
data.translatedDescription: Since this summer's World Cup, the Swedish national team player Elliot Stroud has changed Mjällby in the Allsvenskan for Hull in the Premier League. Already in his debut he got to play against his favorite team. - Every now and then you feel: "What am I really doing here?", says Stroud.

data.title: Alex Schulman: Hatet mot Emil Persson får mig att tappa tron på människosläktet
data.description: För många år sedan hamnade jag i ett hatdrev. Det var hemskt. Sedan dess blir jag extra illa berörd när jag ser andra människor drabbas. Som nu: Emil Persson.
data.translatedTitle: Alex Schulman: The hatred towards Emil Persson makes me lose faith in the human race
data.translatedDescription: Many years ago I got into a hate streak. It was terrible. Since then, I get extra hurt when I see other people affected. Like now: Emil Persson.

data.title: Ledare: Med Tidöpartierna i regering behövs ingen politisk satir
data.description: Kanske blir arvet efter Tidö en förändrad syn på experter och myndigheter, spår SVT:s satirprogram. Det vore i så fall olyckligt – och nästa regering måste kunna bättre än så.
data.translatedTitle: Leader: With the Tidö parties in government, there is no need for political satire
data.translatedDescription: Perhaps the legacy of Tidö will be a changed view of experts and authorities, predicts SVT's satirical program. In that case, it would be unfortunate - and the next government must know better than that.

data.title: Ökad användning av AI – samtidigt längtar fler efter digital detox
data.description: Användningen av AI-tjänster har ökat kraftigt i Sverige det senaste året. Samtidigt upplever allt fler digital trötthet och en längtan efter en paus från det digitala, enligt en ny rapport. – Många berättar om dåligt samvete och svårigheter att sluta, säger Måns Jonasson, på Internetstiftelsen.
data.translatedTitle: Increased use of AI - at the same time, more people yearn for a digital detox
data.translatedDescription: The use of AI services has increased sharply in Sweden in the past year. At the same time, more and more people are experiencing digital fatigue and a longing for a digital break, according to a new report. - Many talk about bad conscience and difficulties in quitting, says Måns Jonasson, at the Internet Foundation.

data.title: Lisa Magnusson: Kvinnor som gör botox är inte problemet
data.description: Jag kan inte tänka mig något mindre feministiskt än att ställa enskilda kvinnor till svars för att de inte är tillräckligt ”bra förebilder”. Jag har en bättre lösning.
data.translatedTitle: Lisa Magnusson: Women who do botox are not the problem
data.translatedDescription: I can't think of anything less feminist than holding individual women accountable for not being "good role models" enough. I have a better solution.

data.title: Så kan din privatekonomi förändras 2027
data.description: I år dopas svenskarnas plånböcker av tillfälliga stimulanser. Nästa år ser kärvare ut. Flera hushåll ser ut att få mindre pengar över, enligt Länsförsäkringars beräkningar. Det återstår att se hur den nya regeringen kan förändra kalkylen.
data.translatedTitle: This is how your personal finances can change in 2027
data.translatedDescription: This year, Swedes' wallets are drugged by temporary stimuli. Next year looks tougher. Several households appear to have less money left over, according to Länsförsäkringar's calculations. It remains to be seen how the new government can change the calculation.

data.title: Vill Sydney Sweeney provocera med flit?
data.description: Hösten 2026 dyker en naken Sydney Sweeney upp i en reklamkampanj för en sportbettingapp. Internet blir rasande. Kritiker menar att Sweeney river upp flera decennier av kvinnorörelse och får tiden att gå bakåt. Det här är inte heller första gången Euphoria-stjärnan hamnar i hetluften. De senaste åren verkar Sweeney medvetet ha försökt stämpla sig själv som sexikon, samtidigt som hon anklagats för att sprida närmast rasideologiska budskap i en kampanj för jeans. Gör hon ogenomtänkta pr-snedsteg – eller vill hon medvetet provocera?
data.translatedTitle: Vill Sydney Sweeney provocera med flit?
data.translatedDescription: In the fall of 2026, a naked Sydney Sweeney appears in an advertising campaign for a sports betting app. The internet goes berserk. Critics believe that Sweeney is tearing up several decades of the women's movement and making time go backwards. This isn't the first time the Euphoria star has come under fire either. In recent years, Sweeney seems to have deliberately tried to brand herself as a sex icon, while being accused of spreading almost racial ideological messages in a campaign for jeans. Is she making ill-considered PR slips - or does she deliberately want to provoke?

data.title: The Proclaimers är fullständigt lysande på Kägelbanan
data.description: Kägelbanan är fullproppad när de skotska tvillingbröderna i The Proclaimers avslutar sin Sverigeturné. Stora delar av konserten är fullständigt lysande, skriver DN:s Mattias Dahlström.
data.translatedTitle: The Proclaimers are absolutely brilliant on the Kägelbanan
data.translatedDescription: The bowling alley is packed when the Scottish twin brothers in The Proclaimers finish their Sweden tour. Large parts of the concert are completely brilliant, writes DN's Mattias Dahlström.

data.title: Laura Misch blomstrar på Faschings scen
data.description: Laura Misch trollbinder publiken med både saxofon och röst. Att scenen inte erbjuder några sceniska effekter att gömma sig bakom är långt ifrån ett problem, skriver DN:s Johanna Paulsson.
data.translatedTitle: Laura Misch flourishes on the Fasching stage
data.translatedDescription: Laura Misch enchants the audience with both saxophone and voice. The fact that the stage does not offer any scenic effects to hide behind is far from a problem, writes DN's Johanna Paulsson.

data.title: Tidigare statssekreteraren: V:s besked upplevs som en krigsförklaring
data.description: Vänsterpartiets vice ordförande Ida Gabrielsson meddelade i SVT:s Agenda på söndagskvällen att de ställer sig bakom Andreas Norlén i måndagens talmansomröstning. Efter beskedet säger den tidigare socialdemokratiska statssekreteraren Irene Wennemo att V:s beslut kommer att upplevas som en krigsförklaring av S.
data.translatedTitle: The former state secretary: V's announcement is perceived as a declaration of war
data.translatedDescription: The Left Party's vice-chairman Ida Gabrielsson announced in SVT's Agenda on Sunday evening that they stand behind Andreas Norlén in Monday's speaker vote. After the announcement, former social democratic state secretary Irene Wennemo says that V's decision will be perceived as a declaration of war by S.

data.title: Källor: Trump överväger basebollplan – i nationalpark
data.description: Donald Trump överväger att låta bygga en basebollplan i en nationalpark, uppger källor för Washington Post. Det ska i första hand handla om Teton National Park i Wyoming.
data.translatedTitle: Sources: Trump Considers Baseball Field - In National Park
data.translatedDescription: Donald Trump is considering building a baseball field in a national park, sources told the Washington Post. It will primarily be about Teton National Park in Wyoming.

data.title: Håller Fox News och Trump på att göra slut?
data.description: Den senaste tiden har den annars så Trumpvänliga tv-kanalen Fox News börjat rikta kritik mot presidenten – gällande allt från Irankriget till presidentens beslut att porta medier från Vita huset. Håller Fox och Trump på att göra slut? – Det finns en efterfrågan på Trumpkritik just nu, säger USA-experten Michael Bossetta.
data.translatedTitle: Are Fox News and Trump Breaking Up?
data.translatedDescription: Recently, the otherwise Trump-friendly TV channel Fox News has begun to direct criticism at the president - regarding everything from the Iran war to the president's decision to port media from the White House. Are Fox and Trump breaking up? - There is a demand for Trump criticism right now, says USA expert Michael Bossetta.

data.title: V stöder Andreas Norlén som talman
data.description: På måndag väljer riksdagen talman. Socialdemokraterna har ännu inte nominerat en kandidat, medan Moderaterna vill se Andreas Norlén fortsätta på posten. I SVT:s Agenda säger Vänsterpartiets vice ordförande Ida Gabrielsson att de kommer att ställa sig bakom Andreas Norlén.
data.translatedTitle: V supports Andreas Norlén as speaker
data.translatedDescription: On Monday, the Riksdag elects the Speaker. The Social Democrats have not yet nominated a candidate, while the Moderates want to see Andreas Norlén continue in office. In SVT's Agenda, the Vice Chair of the Left Party, Ida Gabrielsson, says that they will stand behind Andreas Norlén.

data.title: 27 september: Missa inte dagens nyheter
data.description: Andreas Norlén nominerad i talmansvalet, de säljer sina ägg till barnlösa svenskar och Stefan Holm ångerfull efter attacken vid Bokmässan – här är nyheterna du inte får missa från dagen.
data.translatedTitle: September 27: Don't miss today's news
data.translatedDescription: Andreas Norlén nominated in the Speaker's election, they sell their eggs to childless Swedes and Stefan Holm repentant after the attack at the Book Fair - here are the news you can't miss from the day.

data.title: Två gripna i avloppsmysteriet i New York
data.description: New York-polisen har sedan i våras gäckats av videoklipp på mystiska män utrustade med pannlampor, spadar och vadarbyxor som försvinner ner i stadens avloppssystem på olika platser. Nu har polisen gripit två män misstänkta för olaga intrång.
data.translatedTitle: Two arrested in New York sewer mystery
data.translatedDescription: Since last spring, the New York police have been eluded by videos of mysterious men equipped with headlamps, shovels and waders disappearing into the city's sewer system in various places. Now the police have arrested two men suspected of illegal trespassing.

data.title: Hans Rosén: Maktspel med höga insatser inför talmansvalet
data.description: Måndagens talmansval har utvecklats till ett maktspel mellan blocken, men också inom Magdalena Anderssons tänkta regeringsunderlag. Vem det än blir som vinner valet så väntar en uppgift väl så svår som den talmannen ställdes inför 2018.
data.translatedTitle: Hans Rosén: Power play with high stakes ahead of the Speaker's election
data.translatedDescription: Monday's Speaker's election has developed into a power play between the blocs, but also within Magdalena Andersson's proposed government foundation. Whoever wins the election will have a task just as difficult as that speaker faced in 2018.

data.title: DN Debatt. ”Talmannen måste göra hotet om extraval verkligt”
data.description: DN DEBATT. Valet gav 176 mandat mot 173 – och en total låsning. V kräver ministerposter, C vägrar regera med V. Regeringsformen erbjuder ingen medlare, ingen utväg och bara fyra omröstningar. Om systemet inte ska gå in i väggen måste talmannen ta ett grepp som grundlagsstiftarna aldrig tänkte sig, skriver Johan Welander, tidigare kammarsekreterare i riksdagen.
data.translatedTitle: DN Debate. "The Speaker must make the threat of by-elections real"
data.translatedDescription: DN DEBATE. The election gave 176 mandates against 173 – and a total deadlock. V demands ministerial positions, C refuses to govern with V. The form of government offers no mediator, no way out and only four votes. If the system is not to run into the wall, the Speaker must take an approach that the framers of the constitution never thought of, writes Johan Welander, former chamber secretary in the Riksdag.

data.title: Insändare. Inför folkomröstningar som kan trumfa riksdagen
data.description: INSÄNDARE. Sverige skulle må bra av ett system liknande det schweiziska med bindande folkomröstningar och medborgarinitiativ. Ett visst antal namnunderskrifter ska kunna tvinga fram en omröstning, skriver Rickard Björklund.
data.translatedTitle: Letter to the editor. Ahead of referendums that can trump the Riksdag
data.translatedDescription: LETTER TO THE EDITOR. Sweden would feel good about a system similar to the Swiss one with binding referendums and citizens' initiatives. A certain number of signatures should be able to force a vote, writes Rickard Björklund.

data.title: ”Stadens ljus” är en förunderligt fin och älskvärt fånig föreställning
data.description: När Chaplins romantiska komedi ”Stadens ljus” kommer till liv som musikal på Uppsala stadsteater blir det en elegant hyllning till stumfilmsgenrens hela register av dråplig kroppskomik, slapstick och tokroliga ljudeffekter, skriver Johanna Paulsson.
data.translatedTitle: "City lights" is a wonderfully fine and endearingly silly show
data.translatedDescription: When Chaplin's romantic comedy "City Lights" comes to life as a musical at the Uppsala City Theatre, it will be an elegant tribute to the silent film genre's entire repertoire of deadly body comedy, slapstick and crazy sound effects, writes Johanna Paulsson.

data.title: Mäktig och skakande upplevelse med smak av helvete
data.description: Norske Leander Djønnes roman ”Allt äter” är en gruvlig och grym saga. Maria Schottenius har läst en berättelse nästan helt utan hopp.
data.translatedTitle: Powerful and shaking experience with a taste of hell
data.translatedDescription: Norwegian Leander Djønne's novel "Allt äter" is a gruesome and cruel fairy tale. Maria Schottenius has read a story almost without hope.

data.title: Sprids på X: ”Jag är svensk – Ryssland inte fienden”
data.description: Tusentals identiska inlägg med budskapet att Ryssland inte är västs fiende sprids på X. Poster med samma innehåll spreds även i fjol – då pekades Ryssland ut som ansvarigt. Nu sprids de samtidigt som flera europeiska länder varnar för ett ökat ryskt hot – varningar som Putin avfärdar.
data.translatedTitle: Spread on X: "I'm Swedish - Russia not the enemy"
data.translatedDescription: Thousands of identical posts with the message that Russia is not the enemy of the West are spread on X. Posts with the same content were also spread last year - when Russia was singled out as responsible. Now they are spreading at the same time as several European countries warn of an increased Russian threat – warnings that Putin dismisses.

data.title: J-O Waldner efter Kinas ras: ”Truls kan bli världsetta”
data.description: Är den kinesiska pingismuren på väg att rämna? Frågan är aktuell efter Kinas ras på rankningen den senaste tiden. De oslagbara har plötsligt blivit mänskliga. – Det här är kanon för sporten, säger Jan-Ove Waldner, en av få icke-kinesiska världsettor de senaste 30 åren.
data.translatedTitle: J-O Waldner after China's race: "Truls can become world number one"
data.translatedDescription: Is the Great Wall of China about to collapse? The question is relevant after China's race on the ranking recently. The Unbeatables have suddenly become human. - This is great for the sport, says Jan-Ove Waldner, one of the few non-Chinese world number one in the last 30 years.

data.title: Piratförlagets jättemiss med Guillous censurbok – ”En tankevurpa”
data.description: Jan Guillous förlag skulle äntligen ge ut rätt version av författarens censurerade debutroman. Men det blev fel – och den strukna meningen saknas igen. ”Vi bleknar!!! Vilket generalmisstag!” skriver Ann-Marie Skarp när DN upptäcker felet.
data.translatedTitle: The pirate publisher's giant mistake with Guillou's censorship book - "A thought dump"
data.translatedDescription: Jan Guillou's publishing house would finally publish the correct version of the author's censored debut novel. But it was wrong - and the deleted sentence is missing again. "We're fading!!! What a general mistake!" writes Ann-Marie Skarp when DN discovers the error.

data.title: Mohamed Ali: Avsäger mig inte uppdraget
data.description: Mohamed Abdukardir Ali (V) som varit i rampljuset de senaste veckorna då han kopplats till en utredning om misstänkt valfusk, skriver i ett Facebookinlägg att hans ledighetsansökan inte innebär att han avsäger sig uppdraget som riksdagsledamot. ”Den ska inte heller tolkas som ett erkännande av skuld”, skriver han.
data.translatedTitle: Mohamed Ali: Not resigning the assignment
data.translatedDescription: Mohamed Abdukardir Ali (V), who has been in the spotlight in recent weeks as he has been linked to an investigation into suspected election fraud, writes in a Facebook post that his application for leave does not mean that he is resigning from his role as a member of parliament. "Nor should it be interpreted as an admission of guilt," he writes.

data.title: M nominerar Norlén som talman – SD, KD och L ställer sig bakom
data.description: Tidöpartierna vill behålla Andreas Norlén som riksdagens talman – ett val som även Vänsterpartiet ställer sig bakom.
data.translatedTitle: M nominates Norlén as Speaker - SD, KD and L support
data.translatedDescription: The Tidö parties want to keep Andreas Norlén as Speaker of the Riksdag - a choice that the Left Party also supports.

data.title: Matilda Källén: Skriver Annika Norlin Sveriges bästa låttexter?
data.description: I höst ges hennes låttexter ut i bokform och tolkas på teaterscenen. Men vilka Annika Norlin-rader är egentligen bäst? DN:s Matilda Källén gräver djupt i en av Sveriges främsta låtskatter och hittar texter som alla förtjänar varsin pjäs.
data.translatedTitle: Matilda Källén: Does Annika Norlin write Sweden's best lyrics?
data.translatedDescription: This autumn, her lyrics will be published in book form and interpreted on the stage. But which Annika Norlin lines are actually the best? DN's Matilda Källén digs deep into one of Sweden's foremost song treasures and finds lyrics that all deserve a play.

data.title: Så mycket kostade Pokémonkortet – svenskt rekord
data.description: En miljon kronor – så mycket kostade Sveriges genom tiderna dyraste Pokémonkort. Och rekordinnehavaren har redan hittat en ny köpare. – Jag ska skicka det till en köpare i England för 1,2 miljoner, säger Kevin Chan.
data.translatedTitle: That's how much the Pokémon card cost - a Swedish record
data.translatedDescription: One million kroner - that's how much Sweden's most expensive Pokémon card of all time cost. And the record holder has already found a new buyer. - I will send it to a buyer in England for 1.2 million, says Kevin Chan.

data.title: Kortbedragarens bekännelser efter lyxlivet: ”En kick”
data.description: När han var 15 år hittade Elliot Castro ett bankkort på tåget på väg till skolan. Han föll för frestelsen och betalade resan. Det blev upptakten till år av bedrägerier i mångmiljonklassen, ett liv i lyx och en världsomspännande polisjakt. Nu tipsar den förra storsvindlaren om hur du slipper bli lurad.
data.translatedTitle: The card fraudster's confessions after the life of luxury: "A kick"
data.translatedDescription: When he was 15, Elliot Castro found a bank card on the train on his way to school. He succumbed to the temptation and paid for the trip. It was the prelude to years of multi-million dollar fraud, a life of luxury and a worldwide police manhunt. Now the former big fraudster advises you on how to avoid being cheated.

data.title: ”Here because of hope” kan vara Ezra Collectives bästa skiva hittills
data.description: Jazzkvintetten Ezra Collectives nya skiva är den svängigaste formen av humanism du kommer höra i år, skriver DN:s Magnus Säll och korar ”Here because of hope” till månadens bästa jazzalbum.
data.translatedTitle: "Here because of hope" may be Ezra Collective's best record to date
data.translatedDescription: The jazz quintet Ezra Collective's new record is the most swinging form of humanism you will hear this year, writes DN's Magnus Säll and calls "Here because of hope" the best jazz album of the month.

data.title: Biltillverkarnas vägval mot klimatneutralitet skiljer sig åt
data.description: Visionen att bygga klimatneutrala bilar finns hos flera tillverkare men målen och tidsperspektiven skiljer sig åt. På vägen dit är det dessutom många led som måste tas hänsyn till.
data.translatedTitle: Car manufacturers' path choices towards climate neutrality differ
data.translatedDescription: The vision of building climate-neutral cars exists with several manufacturers, but the goals and time perspectives differ. On the way there, there are also many steps that must be taken into account.

data.title: Liberalernas lokala bakslag i valet blir ekonomisk smäll
data.description: UPPSALA. Jubel och lättnad över riksdagsvalet. Sorg och besvikelse över vad som händer i regioner och på kommunnivå. För Liberalerna är det en ekonomisk smäll att röstas bort från regionpolitiken. Hur ska partiet komma tillbaka?

data.title: Han var den, der ville tage debatten. Nu har han forladt den. Har han fået mundkurv på?
data.description: Martin Rubys egen mor var bekymret, men da den danske chef for Facebook og Instagram begyndte i sit omdiskuterede job, var det med viljen til at træde frem og deltage i den ophedede debat om sociale medier. Nu har politikerne højlydt forladt dialogen, og Martin Ruby selv har nærmest trukket sig fra debatten. Har han fået besked på at holde mund? Og arbejder han stadig i skyggerne?
data.translatedTitle: He was the one who wanted to take the debate. Now he has left it. Has he been muzzled?
data.translatedDescription: Martin Ruby's own mother was worried, but when the Danish head of Facebook and Instagram began his controversial job, it was with the will to step forward and participate in the heated debate about social media. Now the politicians have loudly left the dialogue, and Martin Ruby himself has almost withdrawn from the debate. Has he been told to shut up? And is he still working in the shadows?

data.title: Waarom Den Haag maar blijft vergeten hoe de normalisering van extreemrechts begon
data.description: Inlichtingendiensten waarschuwen voor extreemrechtse groepen die begrippen als ‘omvolking’ en ‘remigratie’ normaliseren. Met goede reden. Toch wringt er iets. Waarom blijft Den Haag maar vergeten wanneer en door wie die normalisering is begonnen?
data.translatedTitle: Why The Hague keeps forgetting how the normalization of the extreme right started
data.translatedDescription: Intelligence services warn against extreme right-wing groups that normalize concepts such as 'repopulation' and 'remigration'. With good reason. Yet something is wrong. Why does The Hague keep forgetting when and by whom this normalization started?

data.title: ‘De explosieve toename van het aantal satellieten is een existentiële bedreiging voor de radiosterrenkunde’
